source.title: Early Stage Convergence and Global Convergence of Training Mildly Parameterized Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no truncation or document mismatch apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves convergence results for two-layer ReLU networks from random initialization and reports CIFAR-10 loss descent, using theoretical bounds and loss measurements rather than the benchmark training-classification-error evaluations in V1.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. for zero training loss but reports no result on that cited work. Its own early-stage loss-descent results do not measure training classification error; the global-convergence theorems and correct-classification lemma bear on V1 under their stated assumptions. CIFAR-10 and MNIST experiments report loss descent only.
record.test_reason: The study proves convergence for fully connected two-layer ReLU networks on specially structured data. V1 concerns convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100. Its CIFAR-10 experiment measures early loss descent, not near-zero classification error. The teacher-student appendix proves early loss descent without measuring spurious-minimum frequency or the benefit of extra student neurons, so it does not test V2. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors establish fast early loss descent for mildly parameterized two-layer networks and global GD convergence under restrictive exponential-type-loss and data assumptions. They also extend early-stage analysis to population risk.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical two-layer ReLU analyses and loss measurements; the reported CIFAR-10 experiment uses a two-layer ReLU network with logistic loss and SGD, rather than the large convolutional benchmark recipes in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: Global-convergence results depend on exponential-type loss, data assumptions, initialization scale, and the prescribed learning-rate schedules. Early-stage descent depends on the specified learning rate and initialization scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 5.2 and 5.3 prove loss convergence from specified random initialization for two-layer ReLU networks on specially separated binary data, with different rates depending on which parameters are trained.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated data, initialization and exponential-type-loss assumptions, adaptive-step GD yields arbitrary polynomial loss convergence when both layers are trained and exponential convergence when only input-layer weights are trained.

fits_no_version.finding: Lemma C.7 establishes correct classification of every training example after the first GD step in the specified binary theoretical setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small random initialization and the paper's separation assumptions allow two-layer ReLU networks trained by GD to classify all training examples correctly after one step and thereafter.

fits_no_version.finding: The paper proves early loss descent and illustrates it on the first 1,000 normalized examples of MNIST and CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the specified initialization, learning-rate and loss assumptions, mildly parameterized two-layer ReLU networks achieve substantial early loss descent within order 1/η iterations.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix E analyzes early population-loss descent in a two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem; it does not compare convergence failures with and without extra student neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the specified Gaussian-input teacher-student problem and small random initialization, GD has a provable early population-loss decrease.

record.problems: The global-convergence theory relies on restrictive loss and data assumptions, which the paper identifies as limitations. The CIFAR-10 experiment uses only the first 1000 normalized examples and reports loss descent rather than classification error; no error bars are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported results were omitted. The MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiment table reports loss descent, which does not measure the training-classification-error behavior named by V1.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error for convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and the stated smaller-model, stopping and regularization qualifications.
Spurious-local-minimum frequency as teacher and student widths grow together, and its reduction with one or two extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts; very deep plain-network and normalization-free residual alternatives.
Effects of activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights on training speed and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial stability threshold, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly says no teacher-student setting is studied: Appendix E contains one, but its early-descent guarantee does not test V2. Restrictive assumptions here are untested scope relative to the supplied versions, not evidence warranting limits_scope. None of the supplied versions receives a verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, convolutional networks, Adam, smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes. CIFAR-10 experiment reports loss descent, not training classification error.
The paper cites spurious-local-minimum work but does not test teacher/student width scaling or outcomes from gradient descent in that setting.
No depth, shortcut, normalization, or plain-network comparison.
No comparison of initialization methods or trainable depth.
